senses.definition: To put a part of yourself against something or come into contact with it.
senses.example: Do not touch the picture until the paint is dry.

senses.definition: To make someone feel a strong emotion, often a warm or sad one.
senses.example: Their kind letter touched me.

senses.definition: The sense that lets you feel something when it makes contact with your body.
senses.example: By touch alone, I could tell which block had a rough edge.

senses.definition: Hard to break, cut, or wear out.
senses.example: We used tough fabric to patch the bag.

senses.definition: Difficult or demanding.
senses.example: The last question on the quiz was tough.

senses.definition: Able to face trouble or pain without giving up easily.
senses.example: She stayed tough during a long, tiring hike.

senses.definition: A trip through a place or several places to look around or learn.
senses.example: We took a tour of the puppet workshop.

senses.definition: To visit parts of a place or several places to look around, teach, or perform.
senses.example: The band will tour small towns this summer.

senses.definition: A piece of cloth or paper used for drying or wiping things.
senses.example: I used a towel to dry my hands.

senses.definition: To dry something by rubbing it with a towel.
senses.example: I toweled my hair before getting on the bus.

senses.definition: A tall, narrow building or structure, often standing by itself or attached to a larger building.
senses.example: A stone tower stood at one end of the old wall.

senses.definition: To stand much higher than other things nearby.
senses.example: Tall pines towered over our tent.

senses.definition: An object made for children to play with or an object used mainly for fun.
senses.example: We took a small toy on the long train ride.

senses.definition: To think briefly about an idea without deciding on it, usually followed by with.
senses.example: We toyed with the idea of making the sign in the shape of a turtle.
